recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (6): github.com/gotify/server/v2.main: main() runs once at start-up (never re-executed / never returns); github.com/gotify/server/v2/router.Create: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v2.main: caller in the call-graph closure never returns; github.com/gotify/server/v2/runner.Run: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing; github.com/gotify/server/v2/runner.Run: caller in the call-graph closure never returns; ... and 1 more
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: github.com/gotify/server/v2/runner.Run is exported: callers outside the analysed module are not in the closure
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 8 functions
1 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (221/222 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
